text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition tells you almost nothing. The person appointed is also a woman, so sex can't plausibly explain why she was preferred over you — there's no differential treatment to point at. An all-women panel in laboratory medicine is also unremarkable; the field is heavily female.

Raising it would likely read as a weak grievance and undercut the point you actually have: you asked for a written explanation two weeks ago and got silence. That's a real procedural failing, and in many jurisdictions you're entitled to reasons.

Chase that in writing, with a deadline. Ask specifically how "broad leadership experience" was assessed against your eight years running a section, and what the scoring was.
